content.text: At Coningsby Castle, Sidonia befriends Coningsby and fascinates Princess Lucretia, while Coningsby’s friendship with Flora and attraction to Lucretia develop amid aristocratic festivities. Sidonia wins a steeplechase, then leaves the Castle for London. Coningsby goes to Cambridge, studies politics, and rejects the hollow Conservative “Cause.” Meanwhile, Millbank defeats Rigby at Darlford. Lord Monmouth marries Lucretia and later settles in Paris with her. Coningsby discovers his mother’s miniature among family papers in London, then travels to Paris, where he meets Edith Millbank and falls deeply in love. Misunderstanding Sidonia’s intimacy with Edith, he leaves Paris for England, later visits Millbank at Oxford and Edith at Hellingsley. Edith and Coningsby confess their love beside the Darl, but Millbank forbids their marriage because of his feud with Lord Monmouth and reveals that Coningsby’s mother had once been loved and abandoned by a Coningsby. Heartbroken, Coningsby returns to his grandfather’s Castle. Nearly four years later, Lord Monmouth urges him to stand as the Conservative candidate for Darlford against Millbank. Coningsby refuses to sacrifice his principles, rejecting party politics without faith, and faces the threatened loss of his grandfather’s support.
